newsitem.title: UK: Yieh Phui board approves bond buyback.
newsitem.headline: Yieh Phui board approves bond buyback.

text.p: Yieh Phui Enterprise Co Ltd's board of directors has approved its plans to buy back a $90 million convertible bond, it said in a statement on Tuesday.
The Taiwanese steel maker said it expected it would take another two weeks to get regulatory approval for the buy back.

"Upon Yieh Phui's receipt of the requisite approvals, bondholders will be notified of the commencement of the tender offer through Euroclear, Cedel and the Depositary Trust Corporation," the statement said, adding the tender offer would remain open for 30 days.
Bankers Trust, lead manager of the deal, would be the repurchasing agent.
There were reports in late June that Yieh Phui had issued fraudulent invoices, a claim it immediately denied.
Yieh Phui had previously said that while it "denies these unfounded allegations ...(it) does want to give investors the choice of selling the convertible bonds back to the company at par."

The convertible notes, with a 10-year maturity and carrying a 1.00 percent coupon, have a conversion price of NT$38.38 per share, which represented a seven percent premium at the time of pricing. The stock was trading at at NT$29.30 on Tuesday.
